before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

before.title: new-app-wizard

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.

# Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "AmberX: approval pop-up not showing, only the Android notification" (amberx-approval-pop-up-not-showing-only-the-android-notification) [bug] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

[ ] s1 (~20m) Trace the veto event path hub -> AmberX and find where the pop-up is dropped

Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step amberx-approval-pop-up-not-showing-only-the-android-notification <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note amberx-approval-pop-up-not-showing-only-the-android-notification "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

before.title: Transparency token works on every dialog and settings window
before.detail:
Root cause: --fx-opacity-glass / opacityGlass only applies where a component's customization has glass:true (framework/core/engines/customize.ts case 'glass'). Settings dialogs and most panels never set it, so the transparency token does nothing there.
Fix: every dialog, settings interface, panel, popover and floating surface uses a token-driven glass background by default (surface mixed with opacityGlass + blur). Add per-surface-type tokens (glass on/off and opacity per surface type: dialog, settings, panel, menu, toolbar, banner) in tokens.style, editable in Token Control and per instance in Quick settings. Rule: everything visual is driven by a token; add a check that fails on hard-coded backgrounds/opacity. Follows skins. Tests, Shipped features.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: every surface must READ the glass/transparency token (wired in everywhere, always), even if it doesn't apply it. Whether a surface actually goes see-through is its own per-surface/per-instance switch (on/off), not missing wiring.

CORRECTION from Brett (replaces the previous note): NO on/off switch. Every surface reads its own transparency token value; the default value is 100% (fully opaque/visible). To make a surface see-through you lower its value. Per surface type tokens in tokens.style, overridable per instance (Quick settings).

before.title: Dispatcher gate: never launch a build that already has a live session
before.detail: Bug seen three times on Nov 13 (ui-manager-floating-window-to-select-any: Earl/Gina, Gina/Paulie, Lenny/Paulie): the orchestrator's dispatcher launched the same build phase twice on the same worktree, so two headless sessions wrote the same files at once. Also 'Self-check: marked running with no session' releases builds back to the Queue while a session is still alive. Fix: (1) a dispatch gate that refuses a launch while ANY live tmux/claude session exists for that build id or worktree (check tmux axf-<build>--*, claude -p pids and a lock file in the worktree); (2) the self-check must confirm a session is really dead (pid + tmux) before releasing; (3) a per-build lock file with heartbeat, where stale locks expire; (4) tests that simulate double dispatch. before.title: Watchdog + watch-rule system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, everything)
before.detail: A server-side watchdog on the VPS that runs every few minutes, checks every orchestrator table (pending, queued, building, merge queue, UI Review) for rows whose build has already landed on main or is otherwise done, and removes or marks them complete automatically. Logs each cleanup and sends an FYI to AmberX.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: I want a server fucking watchdog on the VPS to do that.

split.note: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Design the stale-row contract stale-row@1 in framework/core/stale-rows.mjs: a pure classifier that takes a row (pending, queued, building, merge-queue entry, UI Review item) plus facts (PR merged on main, commits on main, build status complete/failed/cancelled, branch deleted, PR closed) and returns keep | complete | remove with a reason code. Add framework/schemas/stale-row.json for the cleanup log record (row kind, row id, build id, action, reason, evidence, at, by: watchdog)
steps.why: New cross-table contract and log schema that every orchestrator table and the console read

steps.text: Write fixture cases for the classifier (landed via merge queue, landed by direct merge commit, closed unmerged PR, build complete but row still queued, UI Review item whose PR merged, a running build that must stay, a missing-facts row that must stay) plus a check script
steps.why: Fixtures are the contract for the classifier

steps.text: Facts gatherer: framework/cli/stale-facts.mjs reads origin/main (git log --merges, branch heads) and the GitHub PR states through github-token.mjs with ETag caching, so a run costs almost no API calls; returns one facts map keyed by build id / branch / PR
Table readers for builds-store rows: pending, queued and building projections from _claude/builds/store.json via builds-store.mjs, each mapped to classifier input

Table readers for the merge queue (land.mjs queue list / merge-queue.mjs state) and UI Review items (review.mjs list), mapped to classifier input; reached through the capabilities, not folder names, where the framework calls them

Watchdog core apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog.mjs: run = gather facts, read every table, classify, and with --dry-run only print the plan; settings (enabled, interval minutes, dry-run, per-table on/off) in the plugin settings registry

Apply actions: builds store rows marked complete with the merged PR (builds-live.mjs so main sees it at once), merge-queue entries removed through land.mjs queue remove, UI Review items closed as merged; every write under the store lock and journalled, never touching a running build

Cleanup log: append each action as a stale-row@1 record to the plugin dataDir (watchdog/log.jsonl, rotated monthly) plus a build note on the affected build; also a Codebase changes log line per run that did anything

FYI to AmberX: one batched notification per run that cleaned something (count + row list), declared in the plugin's notify.json (notify-types@1) and sent through axf.notify@1 so the Notifications panel controls it
VPS schedule: cron axf-stale-watchdog every 5 minutes running watchdog.mjs run with a lockfile so runs never overlap; install/uninstall in the plugin's install.mjs / uninstall.mjs
Health check: register a health@1 check in the systems check (watchdog last run older than 3 intervals or last run failed = red banner item with Auto fix that reruns it / reinstalls the cron)

API: REST routes /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog (GET status + last runs + log, POST run, POST dry-run, PUT settings), MCP via plugin-commands (watchdog-status, watchdog-run, watchdog-log, watchdog-settings), CLI axf watchdog status|run|log|set, voice actions orchestrator.watchdog.*

UI: a Watchdog card in Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (settings, last run, Run now, Dry run) and a Cleanups log tab using framework controls and TabGroup; register console-control targets (view:…/tab:watchdog, setting:…) and console_show deep link

Tests: unit tests for table readers and apply actions against a temp store, merge-queue and UI Review fixtures (dry-run makes no writes, running builds untouched, second run is a no-op); wire check-stale-rows.mjs into CI

Run checks (check-stale-rows, watchdog tests, builds-store verify, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, plugin-lifecycle check, glossary catalog --check), dry-run on the VPS data and paste its plan, UI Review submit with 3 options, write _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-stale-row-watchdog-vps.md, add the THREADS.md row, open the PR saying how REST/MCP/CLI/voice reach each part

Shared watch-rule engine on the VPS: rules = a pre-built thing to watch + conditions combined with AND / OR (with grouping) + a pre-built action, with values chosen from lists. Reusable by any screen; the stale-row cleanup becomes the first built-in rule.
Collapsible 'Watches' section on the Build orchestrator page listing its rules (expandable rows, on/off, last fired), with an 'Add watch' button.

'Add watch' wizard, zero typing: a grid of pre-built things to watch; selecting one expands the row to pick pre-built conditions and actions from lists and enter values (dropdowns, pickers, number steppers). Plain-English summary of the rule before saving.

AND / OR conditions per watch: '+ add condition' in the wizard, each joined by an AND/OR picker, plus condition groups (e.g. (A AND B) OR C) built by clicking, no typing; the plain-English summary shows the logic.
Same collapsible 'Watches' container with the Add-watch wizard on the Plan Studio page, with Plan Studio's own pre-built things to watch and actions.

A master collapsible 'All watches' container listing every possible thing that can be monitored across the system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, UI Review, merge queue, accounts, VPS, etc.), grouped by area, each addable with one click via the same wizard.

Gates tab in the Watchdog panel: lists every existing gate on the VPS (test gate on landing, UI Review gate, merge approval, budget caps, etc.) as expandable rows with on/off, what it blocks, last triggered; plus 'Add gate' using the same zero-typing wizard (pre-built things to check, AND/OR conditions, pre-built block/notify actions).

Watchdog panel has exactly three tabs: 1) Watches (things being monitored + actions, incl. stale-row cleanup), 2) Gates (everything that blocks/holds work), 3) Rules (every standing rule the VPS enforces, e.g. account routing, auto-merge, rebuild-on-conflict, step splitting). Each tab: count in the tab label, expandable rows, on/off, and an Add button using the same zero-typing wizard.

steps.text: Find where build sessions copy the account login; switch them to the one shared credentials file per account
Write refreshed tokens back to the shared file under a lock so parallel builds don't clobber each other
Test two builds on one account: force a refresh in one, confirm the other keeps working
Phone alert on any OAuth failure and auto re-queue the failed build once the login works

Phone notifications through AmberX for every login event: one each time a build signs in / uses the account token (which account, which build, verified OK or failed), and one each time the token is refreshed confirming the new token was saved to the shared file successfully (or that it failed). Brett: 'anytime something gets in the queue and it attempts to run and it fails, I want an alert and I want to know why.'

steps.text: Design picker@1 contract: picker-model engine spec (options, groups, icons, descriptions, multiple, search threshold, value/labels, open/choose/close state) and the swap contract that replaces native <select>, custom dropdowns and comboboxes, written in framework/spec/PICKER.md with the Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md
steps.why: Cross-port contract that changes how every select behaves across all apps

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/picker.ts: normalise options from a native select / option list, filter by search, group, toggle for single/multi, keyboard model (arrows, home/end, type-ahead, enter, escape), choose-by-name matcher for voice; export it from the core index
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app and the future Kotlin port

steps.text: Golden fixture framework/spec/fixtures/picker.json plus generator and check entries (gen-fixtures.mts, framework/spec/check-picker.mts) covering filter, group, multi toggle, keyboard moves and name matching
steps.why: Conformance fixture is the cross-port contract

steps.text: Register the picker token family in the token registry (surface, backdrop, header, search, option row, hover, focus, selected, disabled, check, group label, sheet handle, radius, padding, gap, every state, light and dark) and make the theme/style engines compile them to --fx-picker-* defaults matching today's dropdown look
steps.why: Schema change to the shared token registry and engine output

steps.text: Add a picker style target to framework/schemas/customize.json (parts box/text/icon/items) so skin-coverage@1 styles it; update the skin upgrader to add picker defaults to every existing skin; run check-skin-coverage.mjs and regenerate fixtures and JSON schemas
steps.why: Skin coverage contract and migration of existing skins

steps.text: Shared React component framework/react/components/PickerField.tsx: field shows current value (and count for multi); tap opens the dialog

Accessibility pass on PickerField/PickerDialog: role=dialog/listbox/option, aria-selected/aria-multiselectable, focus trap and return focus, engine keyboard model wired, labels from the source select; framework controls only

Removable plugin scaffold apps/console-web/plugins/picker-dialog: plugin.json (builtWith, description, lifecycle dataDir, web library that switches pickerSwap on), install.mjs, uninstall.mjs, README; plugin off = original dropdowns

Settings sub-tab under Settings → Plugins → Picker dialog (enable, search threshold, phone sheet on/off, per-app exclusions) with level toolbar, settings asset and control@1 targets registered for console control

API: REST routes in the plugin server (state: enabled, open picker, its options and value; actions: open <target>, choose <option name>, close, settings get/set) with data-axf-target addresses on every picker

API parity: MCP plugin commands, console actions picker.open / picker.choose / picker.close, axf CLI subcommand and AmberX voice phrases ('open the <field> picker', 'choose <option>'), all routed through the same handlers; console_show deep link to the settings tab

Migrate the remaining console plugin dropdowns (second half: apps/console-web/plugins/*/web) to SelectField / PickerField

before.title: Picker dialog plugin replaces all dropdowns
before.detail: New removable plugin: replaces EVERY dropdown/select in the console and framework (native <select>, custom dropdowns, comboboxes) with a tap-to-open picker dialog. The field shows the current value; tapping opens a themed dialog listing the options (search box when many, grouped sections, icons/descriptions if available, multi-select with checkboxes where the select is multiple, keyboard and screen-reader accessible). Fully token-driven: register its own token family (dialog surface, backdrop, option row, selected, hover, focus, search, header, every state, light and dark) in the token registry; no literal colours/sizes (CI gate); every skin can style it and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

steps.why: Reference engine internals with a conformance fixture

Themed color picker dialog: theme swatches, recent colours, hue/saturation area, hex field, keyboard, bottom sheet on phone; swap color inputs
Color picker API (open, set, read) on REST, MCP, CLI and voice, plus control targets

Dialogs API: list open dialogs, answer one (OK/Cancel/text) through REST, MCP, CLI and voice; a dialog that would confirm a destructive action still needs confirm
Themed file drop zone: click to browse, drag and drop, file list, per-file progress bar, accept/multiple respected, keyboard + aria-live upload status; swap file inputs
File drop API: state (files, progress) readable, clear/cancel actions on REST, MCP, CLI and voice
Themed tooltips: move title attributes to data-axf-tip and show a token-styled tooltip on hover/focus (long-press on touch), aria-describedby kept, restored on off

before.title: Land all skin builds
before.detail: Land these one at a time, in order. For each: fetch its remote branch (pull --rebase or merge the remote branch first; build_land push was rejected as non-fast-forward), merge origin/main, resolve conflicts keeping both sides' features, regenerate generated files (generated-files@1), run tests, push, merge to main. Order: skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land (Skins plugin; installing it hides the built-in skins panel, removing it brings it back), skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land, every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme, console-skin-axhub-only, skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out, skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch, token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups. Archive superseded older branches (skins-plugin-own-removable-console, skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes, professional-skins-rebuild-whole-app, fix-merge-conflicts-pr-557-professional) after checking their commits are included. Then run /usr/local/bin/axf-console-update to redeploy, verify the console loads with no doubled chrome, and send Brett a phone notification through AmberX listing what landed.

skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: check out the branch, pull --rebase from its remote branch to clear the non-fast-forward, then merge origin/main. Resolve conflicts and keep both sides' features: the Skins plugin hides the built-in skins panel when installed and brings it back when removed. Commit the merge.

skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: regenerate the generated files (generated-files@1: tracker.mjs, axf.mjs schemas, re-bake the console's src/axf, help/control registries) and commit them. Run the plugin's lifecycle check (install hides the built-in panel, uninstall --all brings it back), check-theme, check-controls and check-skin.mts.

skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: push the branch, link it with builds-live.mjs link, and add its PR to the merge queue with land.mjs queue add. Only the queue merges (Nov 4 rule), so make no direct merge to main.

skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the updated skins-plugin branch tip and origin/main so it stacks cleanly. Resolve conflicts and keep both sides' features (config panel plus the plugin's panel swap). Commit.

skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land: regenerate the generated files, run check-skin.mts, check-console-control.mjs and the console typecheck, push, link and add it to the merge queue behind skins-plugin.

every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous queued tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in framework/assets/skin and the colour-theme assets, keeping both light and dark themes and every skin added on the other side. Commit.

every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme: run shared-assets.mjs bake, regenerate the fixtures and schemas, run theme-swap.mjs, check-skin-coverage.mjs and check-skin.mts, push, link and add it to the merge queue.

console-skin-axhub-only: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the appearance source and skin resolution so the console skin comes only from axHub and per-app skins stay intact. Commit.
console-skin-axhub-only: regenerate the generated files, re-bake the console, run check-skin.mts and the hubstatus tests, push, link and add it to the merge queue.

skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts with console-skin-axhub-only's switch logic, keeping the greyed-out override plus its reason text. Commit.
skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out: regenerate the generated files, run check-console-control.mjs (setting address still callable) and check-skin.mts, push, link and add it to the merge queue.

skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in skin-switch animations and swatches, keeping the opacity and motion tokens from both sides. Commit.
skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: regenerate the generated files, run check-theme.mjs, theme-swap.mjs and check-controls.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.

token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, part 1: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the token registry and control@1 targets: new targets go last, since the registry is append-only. Commit.
token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, part 2: resolve the remaining conflicts in the skin editor and sandbox UI, keeping the config panel's and plugin's features. Commit.

token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox: regenerate the fixtures (gen-fixtures.mts), schemas and tracker, re-bake, run check-control, check-skin.mts and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.

own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the DataGrid and TabGroup token sets and in the tab-group asset, keeping the token registry entries from both sides. Commit.

own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: regenerate the generated files, run check-tab-group.mts, check-chrome-assets.mjs, check-theme.mjs and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.

Watch the merge-queue stack (land.mjs queue list). If an entry goes red, read the failure from the 'CI build errors' issue, fix it on that branch, push and re-add it. Record each merge commit in the report.

Superseded branches: for each of skins-plugin-own-removable-console, skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes, professional-skins-rebuild-whole-app and fix-merge-conflicts-pr-557-professional, list its commits missing from main (git cherry / patch-id). Note any unique work in the report, and stop and flag it instead of archiving if anything real is missing.

Archive the superseded branches that are fully included: push an archive/<name> tag, delete the remote branch, close their PRs with a note naming the PR that replaced them, and mark their builds-store records complete/superseded.

Once all 8 have merged, run /usr/local/bin/axf-console-update. Then verify: the console loads, the Skins plugin panel replaces the built-in one with no doubled chrome (one banner, one skins panel), and capture desktop and phone shots with axf shot into the group 'land-all-skin-builds - <Mon D h:mm AM/PM>'.

Log the deploy with axf_deploy_log (deploy-log@1). Send Brett one phone notification through the AmberX app (axf.notify@1 / alert hub) listing every build that landed with its PR number, and the archived branches.

Wrap-up: run builds-store.mjs verify and tracker.mjs --check, finish the report (_claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md: order, conflicts resolved, tests, PRs, archived branches, deploy check), and update the THREADS.md row. Mark the build complete in the orchestrator, commit through a status PR into the merge queue, and record the changes.mjs result.

For each: fetch its remote branch (pull --rebase or merge the remote branch first; build_land push was rejected as non-fast-forward), merge origin/main, resolve conflicts keeping both sides' features, regenerate generated files (generated-files@1), run tests, push, merge to main. Order: skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land (Skins plugin; installing it hides the built-in skins panel, removing it brings it back), skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land, every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme, console-skin-axhub-only, skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out, skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch, token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups. Archive superseded older branches (skins-plugin-own-removable-console, skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes, professional-skins-rebuild-whole-app, fix-merge-conflicts-pr-557-professional) after checking their commits are included. Then run /usr/local/bin/axf-console-update to redeploy, verify the console loads with no doubled chrome, and send Brett a phone notification through AmberX listing what landed.

# Build: land-all-skin-builds

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-14T18:15:01.485Z
> land the skin builds

## What to build
Continue build "Land all skin builds" (land-all-skin-builds) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-14 18:15):
"land the skin builds"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (25 left, ~3.8 h):
[ ] s1 (~6 min) Survey: fetch origin and list the 8 skin branches plus the 4 superseded ones; for each, record ahead/behind vs origin/main, its open PR number and its builds-store record (builds-store.mjs get / builds-live.mjs). Write the table to the top of _claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md and commit it.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: check out the branch, pull --rebase from its remote branch to clear the non-fast-forward, then merge origin/main. Resolve conflicts and keep both sides' features: the Skins plugin hides the built-in skins panel when installed and brings it back when removed. Commit the merge.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: regenerate the generated files (generated-files@1: tracker.mjs, axf.mjs schemas, re-bake the console's src/axf, help/control registries) and commit them. Run the plugin's lifecycle check (install hides the built-in panel, uninstall --all brings it back), check-theme, check-controls and check-skin.mts.
[ ] s4 (~4 min) skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: push the branch, link it with builds-live.mjs link, and add its PR to the merge queue with land.mjs queue add. Only the queue merges (Nov 4 rule), so make no direct merge to main.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the updated skins-plugin branch tip and origin/main so it stacks cleanly. Resolve conflicts and keep both sides' features (config panel plus the plugin's panel swap). Commit.
[ ] s6 (~10 min) skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land: regenerate the generated files, run check-skin.mts, check-console-control.mjs and the console typecheck, push, link and add it to the merge queue behind skins-plugin.
[ ] s7 (~10 min) every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous queued tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in framework/assets/skin and the colour-theme assets, keeping both light and dark themes and every skin added on the other side. Commit.
[ ] s8 (~10 min) every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme: run shared-assets.mjs bake, regenerate the fixtures and schemas, run theme-swap.mjs, check-skin-coverage.mjs and check-skin.mts, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s9 (~10 min) console-skin-axhub-only: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the appearance source and skin resolution so the console skin comes only from axHub and per-app skins stay intact. Commit.
[ ] s10 (~8 min) console-skin-axhub-only: regenerate the generated files, re-bake the console, run check-skin.mts and the hubstatus tests, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s11 (~10 min) skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts with console-skin-axhub-only's switch logic, keeping the greyed-out override plus its reason text. Commit.
[ ] s12 (~8 min) skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out: regenerate the generated files, run check-console-control.mjs (setting address still callable) and check-skin.mts, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s13 (~10 min) skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in skin-switch animations and swatches, keeping the opacity and motion tokens from both sides. Commit.
[ ] s14 (~10 min) skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: regenerate the generated files, run check-theme.mjs, theme-swap.mjs and check-controls.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s15 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, part 1: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the token registry and control@1 targets: new targets go last, since the registry is append-only. Commit.
[ ] s16 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, part 2: resolve the remaining conflicts in the skin editor and sandbox UI, keeping the config panel's and plugin's features. Commit.
[ ] s17 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox: regenerate the fixtures (gen-fixtures.mts), schemas and tracker, re-bake, run check-control, check-skin.mts and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s18 (~10 min) own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the DataGrid and TabGroup token sets and in the tab-group asset, keeping the token registry entries from both sides. Commit.
[ ] s19 (~10 min) own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: regenerate the generated files, run check-tab-group.mts, check-chrome-assets.mjs, check-theme.mjs and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s20 (~10 min) Watch the merge-queue stack (land.mjs queue list). If an entry goes red, read the failure from the 'CI build errors' issue, fix it on that branch, push and re-add it. Record each merge commit in the report.
[ ] s21 (~8 min) Superseded branches: for each of skins-plugin-own-removable-console, skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes, professional-skins-rebuild-whole-app and fix-merge-conflicts-pr-557-professional, list its commits missing from main (git cherry / patch-id). Note any unique work in the report, and stop and flag it instead of archiving if anything real is missing.
[ ] s22 (~6 min) Archive the superseded branches that are fully included: push an archive/<name> tag, delete the remote branch, close their PRs with a note naming the PR that replaced them, and mark their builds-store records complete/superseded.
[ ] s23 (~10 min) Once all 8 have merged, run /usr/local/bin/axf-console-update. Then verify: the console loads, the Skins plugin panel replaces the built-in one with no doubled chrome (one banner, one skins panel), and capture desktop and phone shots with axf shot into the group 'land-all-skin-builds - <Mon D h:mm AM/PM>'.
[ ] s24 (~5 min) Log the deploy with axf_deploy_log (deploy-log@1). Send Brett one phone notification through the AmberX app (axf.notify@1 / alert hub) listing every build that landed with its PR number, and the archived branches.
[ ] s25 (~10 min) Wrap-up: run builds-store.mjs verify and tracker.mjs --check, finish the report (_claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md: order, conflicts resolved, tests, PRs, archived branches, deploy check), and update the THREADS.md row. Mark the build complete in the orchestrator, commit through a status PR into the merge queue, and record the changes.mjs result.
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md, _claude/builds/store.json, apps/console-web/plugins/skins/, framework/libs/settings/, apps/console-web/src/, tracker.json, framework/schemas/json/, apps/console-web/src/axf/, apps/console-web/plugins/push-banner/land/, framework/react/, framework/assets/skin/, framework/assets/color-theme/, apps/*/src/axf/assets/, framework/spec/fixtures/, framework/core/engines/, framework/libs/hubstatus/, framework/spec/, framework/ui/axf.css, apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs, framework/schemas/, framework/react/components/TabGroup.tsx, framework/react/components/, framework/assets/tab-group/, framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json, deploy/, apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step land-all-skin-builds <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link land-all-skin-builds --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step land-all-skin-builds <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note land-all-skin-builds "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

before.title: Picker dialog plugin replaces all dropdowns
before.detail: New removable plugin: replaces EVERY dropdown/select in the console and framework (native <select>, custom dropdowns, comboboxes) with a tap-to-open picker dialog. The field shows the current value; tapping opens a themed dialog listing the options (search box when many, grouped sections, icons/descriptions if available, multi-select with checkboxes where the select is multiple, keyboard and screen-reader accessible). Fully token-driven: register its own token family (dialog surface, backdrop, option row, selected, hover, focus, search, header, every state, light and dark) in the token registry; no literal colours/sizes (CI gate); every skin can style it and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

origin.said: I want a plugin that replaces all drop down select boxes with a themable dialogue that matches the theme; skins have to touch them; they must conform to the token system

split.note: Split by Claude into 22 steps (5 Fable).

steps.text: Design picker@1 contract: picker-model engine spec (options, groups, icons, descriptions, multiple, search threshold, value/labels, open/choose/close state) and the swap contract that replaces native <select>, custom dropdowns and comboboxes, written in framework/spec/PICKER.md with the Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md
steps.why: Cross-port contract that changes how every select behaves across all apps

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/picker.ts: normalise options from a native select / option list, filter by search, group, toggle for single/multi, keyboard model (arrows, home/end, type-ahead, enter, escape), choose-by-name matcher for voice; export it from the core index
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app and the future Kotlin port

steps.text: Golden fixture framework/spec/fixtures/picker.json plus generator and check entries (gen-fixtures.mts, framework/spec/check-picker.mts) covering filter, group, multi toggle, keyboard moves and name matching
steps.why: Conformance fixture is the cross-port contract

steps.text: Register the picker token family in the token registry (surface, backdrop, header, search, option row, hover, focus, selected, disabled, check, group label, sheet handle, radius, padding, gap, every state, light and dark) and make the theme/style engines compile them to --fx-picker-* defaults matching today's dropdown look
steps.why: Schema change to the shared token registry and engine output

steps.text: Add a picker style target to framework/schemas/customize.json (parts box/text/icon/items) so skin-coverage@1 styles it; update the skin upgrader to add picker defaults to every existing skin; run check-skin-coverage.mjs and regenerate fixtures and JSON schemas
steps.why: Skin coverage contract and migration of existing skins

steps.text: Shared React component framework/react/components/PickerField.tsx: field shows current value (and count for multi); tap opens the dialog

PickerDialog.tsx: themed dialog on desktop, bottom sheet on phone (layout breakpoint token); search box past the threshold, grouped sections, icons and descriptions, checkboxes for multi; tokens only, with styles in framework/ui/axf.css

Accessibility pass on PickerField/PickerDialog: role=dialog/listbox/option, aria-selected/aria-multiselectable, focus trap and return focus, engine keyboard model wired, labels from the source select; framework controls only

Swap layer framework/react/pickerSwap.ts: when enabled, AxfProvider routes framework SelectField/Dropdown/Combobox to PickerField, and a MutationObserver enhances remaining native <select> elements (hidden select kept as the source of truth, change events fired); off restores the originals untouched

Removable plugin scaffold apps/console-web/plugins/picker-dialog: plugin.json (builtWith, description, lifecycle dataDir, web library that switches pickerSwap on), install.mjs, uninstall.mjs, README; plugin off = original dropdowns

Settings sub-tab under Settings → Plugins → Picker dialog (enable, search threshold, phone sheet on/off, per-app exclusions) with level toolbar, settings asset and control@1 targets registered for console control

API: REST routes in the plugin server (state: enabled, open picker, its options and value; actions: open <target>, choose <option name>, close, settings get/set) with data-axf-target addresses on every picker

API parity: MCP plugin commands, console actions picker.open / picker.choose / picker.close, axf CLI subcommand and AmberX voice phrases ('open the <field> picker', 'choose <option>'), all routed through the same handlers; console_show deep link to the settings tab
Migrate the framework's own selects (framework/react, framework/libs/settings) to SelectField so they swap cleanly; grep for raw <select> and custom dropdowns and list leftovers
Migrate the console's custom dropdowns and comboboxes in apps/console-web/src and plugins to SelectField / PickerField (first half: src/views)
Migrate the remaining console plugin dropdowns (second half: apps/console-web/plugins/*/web) to SelectField / PickerField

CI gate framework/cli/check-pickers.mjs: fails on hand-made dropdowns outside SelectField/PickerField, plus check-theme.mjs coverage of picker CSS (no literal colours/sizes); ratchet baseline; wire into CI
Re-bake shared assets and framework into console, axHub web, AmberX and demo (shared-assets.mjs bake, rebake.mjs); run tracker.mjs, schemas, validate --framework

Tests: plugin test (enable/disable restores originals, REST/MCP/CLI/voice open+choose parity), Playwright desktop and phone (sheet, search, multi, keyboard), theme-swap.mjs and a skin swap restyle the picker
Help entry and glossary description, Shipped features ledger rows, plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall
UI Review: 3 picker look options as assets in plugins/picker-dialog/assets/picker/ with desktop + phone shots via review.mjs submit --choices

Run the full check sweep, write _claude/builds/reports/picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all.md (how each feature is reached: deep link, REST, MCP, CLI, voice), THREADS row, push branch, open PR and link it with builds-live.mjs

before.title: Picker dialog plugin replaces all dropdowns
before.detail: New removable plugin: replaces EVERY dropdown/select in the console and framework (native <select>, custom dropdowns, comboboxes) with a tap-to-open picker dialog. The field shows the current value; tapping opens a themed dialog listing the options (search box when many, grouped sections, icons/descriptions if available, multi-select with checkboxes where the select is multiple, keyboard and screen-reader accessible). Fully token-driven: register its own token family (dialog surface, backdrop, option row, selected, hover, focus, search, header, every state, light and dark) in the token registry; no literal colours/sizes (CI gate); every skin can style it and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Picker dialog plugin replaces all dropdowns
before.detail: New removable plugin: replaces EVERY dropdown/select in the console and framework (native <select>, custom dropdowns, comboboxes) with a tap-to-open picker dialog. The field shows the current value; tapping opens a themed dialog listing the options (search box when many, grouped sections, icons/descriptions if available, multi-select with checkboxes where the select is multiple, keyboard and screen-reader accessible). Fully token-driven: register its own token family (dialog surface, backdrop, option row, selected, hover, focus, search, header, every state, light and dark) in the token registry; no literal colours/sizes (CI gate); every skin can style it and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

# Build: land-all-skin-builds

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-14T18:15:01.485Z
> land the skin builds

## What to build
Continue build "Land all skin builds" (land-all-skin-builds) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-14 18:15):
"land the skin builds"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (25 left, ~3.8 h):
[ ] s1 (~6 min) Survey: fetch origin and list the 8 skin branches plus the 4 superseded ones; for each, record ahead/behind vs origin/main, its open PR number and its builds-store record (builds-store.mjs get / builds-live.mjs). Write the table to the top of _claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md and commit it.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: check out the branch, pull --rebase from its remote branch to clear the non-fast-forward, then merge origin/main. Resolve conflicts and keep both sides' features: the Skins plugin hides the built-in skins panel when installed and brings it back when removed. Commit the merge.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: regenerate the generated files (generated-files@1: tracker.mjs, axf.mjs schemas, re-bake the console's src/axf, help/control registries) and commit them. Run the plugin's lifecycle check (install hides the built-in panel, uninstall --all brings it back), check-theme, check-controls and check-skin.mts.
[ ] s4 (~4 min) skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: push the branch, link it with builds-live.mjs link, and add its PR to the merge queue with land.mjs queue add. Only the queue merges (Nov 4 rule), so make no direct merge to main.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the updated skins-plugin branch tip and origin/main so it stacks cleanly. Resolve conflicts and keep both sides' features (config panel plus the plugin's panel swap). Commit.
[ ] s6 (~10 min) skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land: regenerate the generated files, run check-skin.mts, check-console-control.mjs and the console typecheck, push, link and add it to the merge queue behind skins-plugin.
[ ] s7 (~10 min) every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous queued tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in framework/assets/skin and the colour-theme assets, keeping both light and dark themes and every skin added on the other side. Commit.
[ ] s8 (~10 min) every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme: run shared-assets.mjs bake, regenerate the fixtures and schemas, run theme-swap.mjs, check-skin-coverage.mjs and check-skin.mts, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s9 (~10 min) console-skin-axhub-only: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the appearance source and skin resolution so the console skin comes only from axHub and per-app skins stay intact. Commit.
[ ] s10 (~8 min) console-skin-axhub-only: regenerate the generated files, re-bake the console, run check-skin.mts and the hubstatus tests, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s11 (~10 min) skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts with console-skin-axhub-only's switch logic, keeping the greyed-out override plus its reason text. Commit.
[ ] s12 (~8 min) skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out: regenerate the generated files, run check-console-control.mjs (setting address still callable) and check-skin.mts, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s13 (~10 min) skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in skin-switch animations and swatches, keeping the opacity and motion tokens from both sides. Commit.
[ ] s14 (~10 min) skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: regenerate the generated files, run check-theme.mjs, theme-swap.mjs and check-controls.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s15 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, part 1: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the token registry and control@1 targets: new targets go last, since the registry is append-only. Commit.
[ ] s16 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, part 2: resolve the remaining conflicts in the skin editor and sandbox UI, keeping the config panel's and plugin's features. Commit.
[ ] s17 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox: regenerate the fixtures (gen-fixtures.mts), schemas and tracker, re-bake, run check-control, check-skin.mts and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s18 (~10 min) own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the DataGrid and TabGroup token sets and in the tab-group asset, keeping the token registry entries from both sides. Commit.
[ ] s19 (~10 min) own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: regenerate the generated files, run check-tab-group.mts, check-chrome-assets.mjs, check-theme.mjs and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s20 (~10 min) Watch the merge-queue stack (land.mjs queue list). If an entry goes red, read the failure from the 'CI build errors' issue, fix it on that branch, push and re-add it. Record each merge commit in the report.
[ ] s21 (~8 min) Superseded branches: for each of skins-plugin-own-removable-console, skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes, professional-skins-rebuild-whole-app and fix-merge-conflicts-pr-557-professional, list its commits missing from main (git cherry / patch-id). Note any unique work in the report, and stop and flag it instead of archiving if anything real is missing.
[ ] s22 (~6 min) Archive the superseded branches that are fully included: push an archive/<name> tag, delete the remote branch, close their PRs with a note naming the PR that replaced them, and mark their builds-store records complete/superseded.
[ ] s23 (~10 min) Once all 8 have merged, run /usr/local/bin/axf-console-update. Then verify: the console loads, the Skins plugin panel replaces the built-in one with no doubled chrome (one banner, one skins panel), and capture desktop and phone shots with axf shot into the group 'land-all-skin-builds - <Mon D h:mm AM/PM>'.
[ ] s24 (~5 min) Log the deploy with axf_deploy_log (deploy-log@1). Send Brett one phone notification through the AmberX app (axf.notify@1 / alert hub) listing every build that landed with its PR number, and the archived branches.
[ ] s25 (~10 min) Wrap-up: run builds-store.mjs verify and tracker.mjs --check, finish the report (_claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md: order, conflicts resolved, tests, PRs, archived branches, deploy check), and update the THREADS.md row. Mark the build complete in the orchestrator, commit through a status PR into the merge queue, and record the changes.mjs result.
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md, _claude/builds/store.json, apps/console-web/plugins/skins/, framework/libs/settings/, apps/console-web/src/, tracker.json, framework/schemas/json/, apps/console-web/src/axf/, apps/console-web/plugins/push-banner/land/, framework/react/, framework/assets/skin/, framework/assets/color-theme/, apps/*/src/axf/assets/, framework/spec/fixtures/, framework/core/engines/, framework/libs/hubstatus/, framework/spec/, framework/ui/axf.css, apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs, framework/schemas/, framework/react/components/TabGroup.tsx, framework/react/components/, framework/assets/tab-group/, framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json, deploy/, apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step land-all-skin-builds <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link land-all-skin-builds --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step land-all-skin-builds <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note land-all-skin-builds "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

before.detail: New removable plugin: replaces EVERY dropdown/select in the console and framework (native <select>, custom dropdowns, comboboxes) with a tap-to-open picker dialog. The field shows the current value; tapping opens a themed dialog listing the options (search box when many, grouped sections, icons/descriptions if available, multi-select with checkboxes where the select is multiple, keyboard and screen-reader accessible). Fully token-driven: register its own token family (dialog surface, backdrop, option row, selected, hover, focus, search, header, every state, light and dark) in the token registry; no literal colours/sizes (CI gate); every skin can style it and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

before.title: Skin from axHub: Override switch, greyed-out editors with notes
before.detail:
Follow-up to console-skin-axhub-only (the 'Get my skin only from axHub' switch in Settings > Appearance).
- Under that switch add an 'Override' switch, off by default. The two are mutually exclusive: turning Override on turns 'Inherit from axHub only' off right away, and turning axHub-only back on turns Override off.
- While axHub-only is on and Override is off, nothing about the skin or its assets can be edited anywhere: every screen, panel, inline editor, UI Manager row and property/token field that would change the skin or an asset is greyed out (disabled, not hidden).
- Each greyed-out area shows a note: 'This is locked: your skin and assets come from axHub. You can still edit it, but if you do it will no longer refresh or inherit any of its data from axHub.' with a 'Click here to override' link.
- Clicking the link (or the Override switch) asks for one confirm, then turns Override on (axHub-only off) and unlocks editing. Edited assets are marked as overridden.
- Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help, Shipped features.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: reuse the existing overridden-settings dialog (the 'N assets controlled by own settings' notice/dialog), don't build a new one. Next to the Override switch, show a hook/link with the count, e.g. '3 tokens overridden', that opens that dialog listing every overridden token and asset, with reset to axHub per item and reset all.

Brett CHANGED this (overrides the detail): the two switches are NOT mutually exclusive. Both 'Inherit from axHub only' and 'Override' can be on together. With both on, the skin keeps inheriting and refreshing from axHub EXCEPT the tokens Brett has edited: only those overridden tokens stop inheriting, and each is marked 'overridden' with 'reset to axHub'. With axHub-only on and Override off, editors are greyed out with the note and a 'click here to override' link that turns Override on.

before.detail:
Follow-up to console-skin-axhub-only (the 'Get my skin only from axHub' switch in Settings > Appearance).
- Under that switch add an 'Override' switch, off by default. The two are mutually exclusive: turning Override on turns 'Inherit from axHub only' off right away, and turning axHub-only back on turns Override off.
- While axHub-only is on and Override is off, nothing about the skin or its assets can be edited anywhere: every screen, panel, inline editor, UI Manager row and property/token field that would change the skin or an asset is greyed out (disabled, not hidden).
- Each greyed-out area shows a note: 'This is locked: your skin and assets come from axHub. You can still edit it, but if you do it will no longer refresh or inherit any of its data from axHub.' with a 'Click here to override' link.
- Clicking the link (or the Override switch) asks for one confirm, then turns Override on (axHub-only off) and unlocks editing. Edited assets are marked as overridden.
- Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help, Shipped features.

Brett: reuse the existing overridden-settings dialog (the 'N assets controlled by own settings' notice/dialog), don't build a new one. Next to the Override switch, show a hook/link with the count, e.g. '3 tokens overridden', that opens that dialog listing every overridden token and asset, with reset to axHub per item and reset all.

Brett CHANGED this (overrides the detail): the two switches are NOT mutually exclusive. Both 'Inherit from axHub only' and 'Override' can be on together. With both on, the skin keeps inheriting and refreshing from axHub EXCEPT the tokens Brett has edited: only those overridden tokens stop inheriting, and each is marked 'overridden' with 'reset to axHub'. With axHub-only on and Override off, editors are greyed out with the note and a 'click here to override' link that turns Override on.
