before.title: Token registry and Skin Editor: live sandbox preview, snapshot history
before.detail:
Runs after the token schema step of own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups (builds on its schema).
1. TOKEN REGISTRY: one registry listing every token in the system, with element type, area (layout/style/colour/behaviour), state, light/dark, level (basic/pro/advanced), plain-English description, default and source. Every new UI, component or plugin MUST register its tokens through its manifest. A CI check fails any UI whose tokens aren't in the registry, and any registered token that nothing uses. Browsable and searchable, with full API.
2. SKIN EDITOR (plugin and screen): pick any UI from the list (a screen, plugin, dialog, element), or pick it on screen, and it's loaded into a sandbox live-preview window with real components and sample data. Every edit hot-renders the preview in real time. The token list comes from the registry, with Basic/Pro/Advanced views. Inline element and asset editors work inside it.
3. DEFAULT SKIN: there is always a built-in default skin that is locked.
4. SNAPSHOTS: every edit to a skin automatically takes a snapshot (like a disk snapshot). A timeline shows the chain of edits, each with time, who/what made it, and a diff of exactly which tokens changed (old -> new). Click any snapshot to preview it, compare any two, or revert to it (a revert is itself a new snapshot, so nothing is ever lost). No breaking skins into separate style or colour groups: the skin is the only unit.
5. EXPORT: at any point, 'Export current to new skin' saves the current state as a brand-new skin (name, thumbnail, to the hub library).
6. Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub work through the snapshots.
7. Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice ('revert the skin to 10 minutes ago', 'export this as a new skin called Midnight'). Tests, help, Shipped features. Fable for the registry and snapshot schema.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: not just individual toolbars, tab groups and menus. Every UI as a whole (each screen, plugin, dialog and app) also gets its own settings interface that changes only that UI, and a DEFAULT STATE: a saved, known-good baseline of its layout, style, colours and behaviour. 'Reset to default' snaps it back, and the default state is itself snapshotted and versioned like skins. Hierarchy: skin -> UI default -> per-UI settings -> per-instance (toolbar/tab group/menu) settings; each level shows what it overrides. Registered in the token registry. Full API and voice.

(4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. split.note: Split by Claude into 20 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Wait gate: check land-all-skin-builds is complete/merged (builds-store get + git log origin/main for skins, skin-axhub-override, axHub-only look code); if not landed, stop and requeue with a note. Record the baseline commit in the report draft.

Capture the live console look as data: read the hub appearance@1 doc and the console's app-look@1 (shared/settings/looks/console.json), the active skin, colour theme light+dark, style theme tokens (incl. opacityGlass 0.7), typography/scale, density, radius, behaviour/animation themes, and chrome settings (toolbar/banner/nav/tab-group axf.chrome.*). Write a raw snapshot JSON for the build.
Before pixel baseline: shoot the live console (desktop + phone, light + dark, main views) with rebuild-shots.mjs at the baseline commit, stored as the pixel-diff reference.

Contract design: define 'hub default skin' in skin@1 / appearance@1 (a `defaultSkin` pointer on the shared appearance document, skin `chrome` block for chrome settings, `backups` record shape per app) and the resolve order hub default → app override tokens → screen → plugin in resolveLookSkin; update asset-types.json and APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md.
steps.why: Schema + cross-app contract change to how every app resolves its look

steps.text: Engine: implement hub-default resolution in the skin/look engine (apps with no override inherit the hub default; apps with edits keep only edited tokens per skin-axhub-override rules) plus the per-app backup/restore record; regenerate JSON schemas.
steps.why: Engine internals of the cross-app look resolver

steps.text: Fixtures + checks: add golden cases (no override, partial override, restore from backup) to framework/spec/fixtures and extend check-skin.mts / check-skin-coverage.mjs; regenerate fixtures; record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md.
steps.why: Conformance contract for the cross-port engine

steps.text: Create the skin asset 'Console (default)' (framework/assets/skin/console-default.json) from the snapshot, exact values; validate with axf validate --framework and confirm a compile of it reproduces the snapshot tokens 1:1 (script diff, zero differences).
Bake the new skin into every shared-assets app (shared-assets.mjs bake) and re-bake console/AmberX/axHub web/Expenses src/axf via rebake.mjs; run shared-assets check and chrome-settings check.

CLI: skins.mjs `default set <skin>|get`, `backup <app>`, `restore <app>`, and `snapshot --from <app> --as <id>` (capture the current look as a skin); backups written to each app's app-look@1 before any switch.

Server routes: theme-manager REST `GET/POST default-skin`, `POST snapshot`, `GET backups/<app>`, `POST restore/<app>`; MCP via plugin-commands; console actions `skin.default`, `skin.snapshot`, `skin.restoreBackup` with voice phrases ('make this the default look', 'restore my old look').

UI: Settings → Appearance (AppearancePanel) gets 'Make this the default look' button (confirm), a 'Default: Console (default)' badge, and 'Restore previous skin' one-tap per app; framework controls/tokens only, control@1 targets registered.

API parity for the UI: deep links (console_show view:settings/tab:appearance target default-skin, restore), state read (default skin + per-app inherit/override/backup), console-control registration; check-console-control.mjs passes.

Publish: back up every app's current skin/app-look on the hub, then set the hub's appearance defaultSkin to 'console-default' and switch each app to inherit (override-only apps keep only their edited tokens). Record the backups list in the report.
Android apps: ensure AmberX droid (allowed exception) reads the hub default through its web shell; record other Android apps' pickup as deferred per the Android hold, no new Kotlin.

Pixel-diff: shoot the console after (same views, desktop + phone, light + dark) and diff against the before set; must be identical (zero changed pixels beyond antialias threshold) — fix any token drift and repeat.

Screenshot every app (console, AmberX web, axHub web, Molly, Expenses, demo) desktop + phone with axf shot into group 'console-look-becomes-default-axhub-skin - <date time>'; submit the new Appearance controls to UI Review with 3 options as assets (button placement variants).
Help + glossary + Shipped features: help entries for the default skin and restore, asset description, catalog.mjs --check, feature-ledger rows; update status.json and tracker.mjs.

Tests: unit tests for skins.mjs default/backup/restore, route tests for theme-manager, check-skin.mts, check-skin-coverage.mjs, check-theme.mjs, check-controls.mjs, check-toolbars.mjs, theme-swap.mjs; fix failures.

Redeploy the console (axf console refresh / nightly deploy path), log with axf_deploy_log, then send Brett one phone notification through axf.notify@1 ('Console look is now the default axHub skin; every app inherits it').

Report _claude/builds/reports/console-look-becomes-default-axhub-skin.md (snapshot, contract changes, backups, pixel-diff result, shots, API/voice table of how each feature is reached), THREADS.md row, STATUS.md line, commit, push, open PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add to the merge queue.

origin.said: We need to make sure things are landing as soon as they're built and merged as soon as they're built. I keep getting too many commits behind

split.note: Split by Claude into 28 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Add 'behind' fields to builds@1 (behindMain count, behindCheckedAt, finishedAt, landState: waiting|landing|landed|red|archived|flagged, landAttempts[]) in framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs + builds-store normaliser, so normBuild keeps them; add a migration that leaves old records untouched; update framework/spec/check-builds-store.mjs cases
steps.why: builds@1 schema + migration design read by every build view and writer

steps.text: Define land-run@1 record (one serial landing attempt: build, base sha, merged sha, regenerated files, check result, ci conclusion incl. cancelled≠failure, outcome, fixBuild id) as a pure core module with a validator and a fixture
steps.why: new cross-tool contract the lander, console, MCP and voice all read

steps.text: Audit the two finished-but-unlanded auto-land builds and replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing: list their branches, diff against main, note what each adds and where they overlap; write findings at the top of the report
Combine the three branches into this build's branch: merge auto-land-every-finished-build-lands, then auto-land-merge-main-land-land-mjs-clash, resolving land.mjs clashes; commit
Merge replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing on top, keep the serial lander path, drop stacking code paths behind it; commit
Serial lander core: land-one.mjs takes one finished build, merges origin/main into its branch, records a land-run@1, refuses to run two at once (lock file); unit test with a temp git repo
Wire regeneration into land-one: run generated-files@1 regenerate after the merge and call /opt/axf-batch/resolve.py for conflicted generated files; commit the result on the branch

Checks once + merge: land-one triggers or waits for CI on the merged head, treats cancelled runs as re-dispatch (never failure), merges to main on green through the GitHub App token, marks build complete via builds-live
Red check path: on a failed check, file a fix build in the orchestrator (said = Brett's verbatim words + the failing check), set landState red, move to the next build; test

Land on finish: build-hook@1 listener on status 'built' enqueues the build into the serial lander at once; cron axf-auto-land runs land-one serially; turn autoLand on by default in serial mode and record the decision
Drift keeper: every 30 min merge origin/main into each running build's branch (skip when the worktree is dirty or a session holds a lock), regenerate generated files, push; record behindMain; test

Dispatcher diagnosis: run pipeline.mjs tick with tracing against the live store and agent-slots status, find why queued builds don't fill 6 of 8 slots (account/model routing, slot accounting, stale locks); write the cause in the report
Fix the dispatcher so it launches until slots or accounts run out in one tick, and add a regression test reproducing the empty-slots case

Backlog list: backlog.mjs lists every built/unlanded build with behindMain, priority and age, ordered newest + most-wanted first with the named builds pinned to the top (move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr, change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console, console app parts 1-4, wake listener, voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected)

Supersede check: for each backlog build, compute unique work (commits/patches not in main via git cherry + file-level diff); superseded = tag archive/<name>, close PR, mark archived; unique = landState flagged with the unique files; test on a temp repo
Land the AmberX web app into the console builds (move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr, change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console) with land-one; log outcomes
Land console app parts 1-4 and the wake listener with land-one, one at a time; log outcomes
Land voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected; then redeploy the console (axf-console-update) and check for doubled chrome with axf shot on desktop + phone
Backlog batch 2: run supersede over the remaining builds, archive the superseded ones, flag the unique ones; log the list
Backlog batch 3: start the serial lander over the rest of the unique builds (it continues by itself), log what landed so far and what went red with fix builds
Redeploy per batch: after each lander batch the lander calls axf-console-update once and runs a doubled-chrome check (one banner, one menu bar in the built console); test the batch boundary
Commits-behind column: show behindMain + landState on every build row (Build manager, Pipeline, Pending, orchestrator grids) via a shared framework cell, tokens only; register control@1 targets

Unlanded alert: a health@1 check in systems-check goes red when a finished build sits unlanded > 15 min (auto-fix = enqueue in the lander), pushed once to the AmberX app through axf.notify@1; declare it in notify.json
Landing summary notification: after each batch send Brett a phone notification through AmberX (axf.notify@1) listing landed / archived / flagged / red

API: REST routes for lander status, backlog, land one, archive, flag, keep-fresh run, dispatcher state (/api/plugins/push-banner/land/*) + deep links (console_show targets for the backlog view and a build's landing row)
API parity: MCP plugin commands, axf CLI subcommands (axf land status|backlog|one|archive|fresh) and AmberX voice actions mapped to the same routes; test that all four call the same handlers

Help + Shipped features: help pages for the serial lander, drift keeper, commits-behind column and unlanded alert; descriptions for new CLIs; glossary catalog check passes; shipped-features rows via build-hook

Tests, report (_claude/builds/reports/land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog.md with what landed, archived, flagged, the dispatcher cause and API reach), UI Review submission with 3 options for the commits-behind column, THREADS row, PR via the merge queue

before.title: Console look becomes default axHub skin
before.detail: Snapshot the live console's current look exactly as it is now (skin, colour theme light and dark, every token value including opacityGlass 0.7, typography, density, radius, behaviour/animation themes, toolbar/banner/nav chrome settings) into a new skin asset 'Console (default)' and publish it on axHub as THE default skin. Make every app (console, AmberX web, Android apps, any app built from the framework) inherit its skin from axHub's default right now: apps with no override pick it up immediately; apps with their own edits keep only their edited tokens (per the skin-axhub-override rules) and inherit the rest. Keep a backup of each app's previous skin so it can be restored in one tap. Run AFTER land-all-skin-builds finishes so it builds on the landed skins plugin/axHub-only/override code; if those aren't landed yet, wait for them. Verify with pixel-diff that the console looks identical before and after, and screenshot every app desktop and phone. Redeploy, then send Brett a phone notification. Full API and voice ('make this the default look'), tests, help, Shipped features.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett override: NO backups of each app's previous skin. Drop that. From now on every 'restore'/'reset to default' anywhere (skins, tokens, per-app, per-element, 'Restore from axHub') restores to this new 'Console (default)' look. It becomes the locked default skin that all resets point at.
Split by Claude into 20 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Keep the design, all the style, the way the console looks right now, and make it the default axHub look, and then make all the apps inherit it right now

split.note: Split by Claude into 20 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Wait gate: check land-all-skin-builds is complete/merged (builds-store get + git log origin/main for skins, skin-axhub-override, axHub-only look code); if not landed, stop and requeue with a note. Record the baseline commit in the report draft.

Capture the live console look as data: read the hub appearance@1 doc and the console's app-look@1 (shared/settings/looks/console.json), the active skin, colour theme light+dark, style theme tokens (incl. opacityGlass 0.7), typography/scale, density, radius, behaviour/animation themes, and chrome settings (toolbar/banner/nav/tab-group axf.chrome.*). Write a raw snapshot JSON for the build.
Before pixel baseline: shoot the live console (desktop + phone, light + dark, main views) with rebuild-shots.mjs at the baseline commit, stored as the pixel-diff reference.

Contract design: define 'hub default skin' in skin@1 / appearance@1 (a `defaultSkin` pointer on the shared appearance document, skin `chrome` block for chrome settings, `backups` record shape per app) and the resolve order hub default → app override tokens → screen → plugin in resolveLookSkin; update asset-types.json and APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md.
steps.why: Schema + cross-app contract change to how every app resolves its look

steps.text: Engine: implement hub-default resolution in the skin/look engine (apps with no override inherit the hub default; apps with edits keep only edited tokens per skin-axhub-override rules) plus the per-app backup/restore record; regenerate JSON schemas.
steps.why: Engine internals of the cross-app look resolver

steps.text: Fixtures + checks: add golden cases (no override, partial override, restore from backup) to framework/spec/fixtures and extend check-skin.mts / check-skin-coverage.mjs; regenerate fixtures; record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md.
steps.why: Conformance contract for the cross-port engine

steps.text: Create the skin asset 'Console (default)' (framework/assets/skin/console-default.json) from the snapshot, exact values; validate with axf validate --framework and confirm a compile of it reproduces the snapshot tokens 1:1 (script diff, zero differences).
Bake the new skin into every shared-assets app (shared-assets.mjs bake) and re-bake console/AmberX/axHub web/Expenses src/axf via rebake.mjs; run shared-assets check and chrome-settings check.

CLI: skins.mjs `default set <skin>|get`, `backup <app>`, `restore <app>`, and `snapshot --from <app> --as <id>` (capture the current look as a skin); backups written to each app's app-look@1 before any switch.

Server routes: theme-manager REST `GET/POST default-skin`, `POST snapshot`, `GET backups/<app>`, `POST restore/<app>`; MCP via plugin-commands; console actions `skin.default`, `skin.snapshot`, `skin.restoreBackup` with voice phrases ('make this the default look', 'restore my old look').

UI: Settings → Appearance (AppearancePanel) gets 'Make this the default look' button (confirm), a 'Default: Console (default)' badge, and 'Restore previous skin' one-tap per app; framework controls/tokens only, control@1 targets registered.

API parity for the UI: deep links (console_show view:settings/tab:appearance target default-skin, restore), state read (default skin + per-app inherit/override/backup), console-control registration; check-console-control.mjs passes.

Publish: back up every app's current skin/app-look on the hub, then set the hub's appearance defaultSkin to 'console-default' and switch each app to inherit (override-only apps keep only their edited tokens). Record the backups list in the report.
Android apps: ensure AmberX droid (allowed exception) reads the hub default through its web shell; record other Android apps' pickup as deferred per the Android hold, no new Kotlin.

Pixel-diff: shoot the console after (same views, desktop + phone, light + dark) and diff against the before set; must be identical (zero changed pixels beyond antialias threshold) — fix any token drift and repeat.

Screenshot every app (console, AmberX web, axHub web, Molly, Expenses, demo) desktop + phone with axf shot into group 'console-look-becomes-default-axhub-skin - <date time>'; submit the new Appearance controls to UI Review with 3 options as assets (button placement variants).
Help + glossary + Shipped features: help entries for the default skin and restore, asset description, catalog.mjs --check, feature-ledger rows; update status.json and tracker.mjs.

Tests: unit tests for skins.mjs default/backup/restore, route tests for theme-manager, check-skin.mts, check-skin-coverage.mjs, check-theme.mjs, check-controls.mjs, check-toolbars.mjs, theme-swap.mjs; fix failures.

Redeploy the console (axf console refresh / nightly deploy path), log with axf_deploy_log, then send Brett one phone notification through axf.notify@1 ('Console look is now the default axHub skin; every app inherits it').

Report _claude/builds/reports/console-look-becomes-default-axhub-skin.md (snapshot, contract changes, backups, pixel-diff result, shots, API/voice table of how each feature is reached), THREADS.md row, STATUS.md line, commit, push, open PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add to the merge queue.

before.title: Land on finish: auto-land live, clear backlog
before.detail: Root cause: the auto-land builds (auto-land-every-finished-build-lands, auto-land-merge-main-land-land-mjs-clash) finished but never landed, so nothing lands by itself; 87 finished builds sit unlanded, many 1,000-2,000 commits behind main. Do, in order: (1) Land the auto-land code first, combined with replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing: a serial lander that, the moment a build finishes, merges origin/main into it, regenerates generated files (generated-files@1, wire /opt/axf-batch/resolve.py too), runs its checks once and merges it to main; no stacking; a cancelled CI run never counts as a failure; on a red check it files a fix build and moves on. While a build is running, merge main into it every 30 min so it never drifts far behind. (2) Fix the dispatcher: 6 of 8 slots sit empty while builds are queued; find why queued builds don't launch and fix it, with a test. (3) Clear the backlog: land every finished build one at a time, newest and most-wanted first, starting with move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr and change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console (AmberX web app into the console), the console app parts 1-4 and wake listener, and voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected. Builds that are fully superseded get archived (tag archive/<name>) after checking no unique work is lost; anything with unique work gets flagged. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. Send Brett a phone notification with a summary of what landed. Full API and voice, tests, help, Shipped features.

origin.brief:
# Build: land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-14T22:17:37.935Z
> We need to make sure things are landing as soon as they're built and merged as soon as they're built. I keep getting too many commits behind

## What to build
Continue build "Land on finish: auto-land live, clear backlog" (land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-14 22:17):
"We need to make sure things are landing as soon as they're built and merged as soon as they're built. I keep getting too many commits behind"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Capture the live console look as data: read the hub appearance@1 doc and the console's app-look@1 (shared/settings/looks/console.json), the active skin, colour theme light+dark, style theme tokens (incl. opacityGlass 0.7), typography/scale, density, radius, behaviour/animation themes, and chrome settings (toolbar/banner/nav/tab-group axf.chrome.*). Write a raw snapshot JSON for the build.
Before pixel baseline: shoot the live console (desktop + phone, light + dark, main views) with rebuild-shots.mjs at the baseline commit, stored as the pixel-diff reference.

Contract design: define 'hub default skin' in skin@1 / appearance@1 (a `defaultSkin` pointer on the shared appearance document, skin `chrome` block for chrome settings, `backups` record shape per app) and the resolve order hub default → app override tokens → screen → plugin in resolveLookSkin; update asset-types.json and APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md.
steps.why: Schema + cross-app contract change to how every app resolves its look

steps.text: Engine: implement hub-default resolution in the skin/look engine (apps with no override inherit the hub default; apps with edits keep only edited tokens per skin-axhub-override rules) plus the per-app backup/restore record; regenerate JSON schemas.
steps.why: Engine internals of the cross-app look resolver

steps.text: Fixtures + checks: add golden cases (no override, partial override, restore from backup) to framework/spec/fixtures and extend check-skin.mts / check-skin-coverage.mjs; regenerate fixtures; record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md.
steps.why: Conformance contract for the cross-port engine

steps.text: Create the skin asset 'Console (default)' (framework/assets/skin/console-default.json) from the snapshot, exact values; validate with axf validate --framework and confirm a compile of it reproduces the snapshot tokens 1:1 (script diff, zero differences).
Bake the new skin into every shared-assets app (shared-assets.mjs bake) and re-bake console/AmberX/axHub web/Expenses src/axf via rebake.mjs; run shared-assets check and chrome-settings check.

CLI: skins.mjs `default set <skin>|get`, `backup <app>`, `restore <app>`, and `snapshot --from <app> --as <id>` (capture the current look as a skin); backups written to each app's app-look@1 before any switch.

Server routes: theme-manager REST `GET/POST default-skin`, `POST snapshot`, `GET backups/<app>`, `POST restore/<app>`; MCP via plugin-commands; console actions `skin.default`, `skin.snapshot`, `skin.restoreBackup` with voice phrases ('make this the default look', 'restore my old look').

UI: Settings → Appearance (AppearancePanel) gets 'Make this the default look' button (confirm), a 'Default: Console (default)' badge, and 'Restore previous skin' one-tap per app; framework controls/tokens only, control@1 targets registered.

API parity for the UI: deep links (console_show view:settings/tab:appearance target default-skin, restore), state read (default skin + per-app inherit/override/backup), console-control registration; check-console-control.mjs passes.

Publish: back up every app's current skin/app-look on the hub, then set the hub's appearance defaultSkin to 'console-default' and switch each app to inherit (override-only apps keep only their edited tokens). Record the backups list in the report.
Android apps: ensure AmberX droid (allowed exception) reads the hub default through its web shell; record other Android apps' pickup as deferred per the Android hold, no new Kotlin.

Pixel-diff: shoot the console after (same views, desktop + phone, light + dark) and diff against the before set; must be identical (zero changed pixels beyond antialias threshold) — fix any token drift and repeat.

Screenshot every app (console, AmberX web, axHub web, Molly, Expenses, demo) desktop + phone with axf shot into group 'console-look-becomes-default-axhub-skin - <date time>'; submit the new Appearance controls to UI Review with 3 options as assets (button placement variants).
Help + glossary + Shipped features: help entries for the default skin and restore, asset description, catalog.mjs --check, feature-ledger rows; update status.json and tracker.mjs.

Tests: unit tests for skins.mjs default/backup/restore, route tests for theme-manager, check-skin.mts, check-skin-coverage.mjs, check-theme.mjs, check-controls.mjs, check-toolbars.mjs, theme-swap.mjs; fix failures.

Redeploy the console (axf console refresh / nightly deploy path), log with axf_deploy_log, then send Brett one phone notification through axf.notify@1 ('Console look is now the default axHub skin; every app inherits it').

Report _claude/builds/reports/console-look-becomes-default-axhub-skin.md (snapshot, contract changes, backups, pixel-diff result, shots, API/voice table of how each feature is reached), THREADS.md row, STATUS.md line, commit, push, open PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add to the merge queue.

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

before.title: Replace merge queue with one-at-a-time landing
before.detail: Brett overrides the Nov 4 'only the queue merges' rule. Remove the batched/stacked merge queue (push-banner land.mjs rounds) and replace it with a serial lander: take one finished build, merge origin/main into it, regenerate generated files (generated-files@1), run its checks once, merge it to main, then the next. No stacking builds on each other, so a fix to one never restarts the others' tests. A cancelled CI run (superseded by a push) is never counted as a failure. On a red check, auto-file a fix build and move on to the next build instead of blocking the line. Show the landing line and its current build in the console with full API and voice control (pause, skip, move up). Redeploy the console after each landing batch. Tests, help, Shipped features.

steps.why: Data migration of a live store

steps.text: Engine checks for landing-line@1: transitions, cancelled-run classification (cancelled / superseded / stale head = retry, failure / timed_out = red), red → fix-file + advance, pause / skip / move-up ordering, migration fixture
steps.why: Conformance checks for the new contract

steps.text: Serial lander, part 1: apps/console-web/plugins/push-banner/land/lander.mjs takes the head entry, checks out its branch, merges origin/main into it, and sets the entry state; reuses the merge drivers already in land.mjs (builds files newer-wins, logs unioned)
Serial lander, part 2: run generated-files@1 regeneration (tracker, schemas, fixtures, help, exports) after the main merge and push the branch once (head pinned)

Red check handling: on a real failure, file a fix build in the orchestrator (pipeline.mjs intake with the failing check names, log excerpt, PR link and Brett's original words carried over), mark the entry fix-filed, link the fix build, then move on to the next entry

Settings sub-tab: Settings → Plugins → Push banner → Landing line (enabled, re-dispatch on cancelled, auto file fix build, redeploy after batch) through the settings asset; remove the stack settings

Systems check: health@1 item when the line is paused over an hour, a landing is stuck in one stage over 30 min, or a fix build was filed (banner item with Fix / Resume); notify.json entry for landing alerts

Rules and docs: replace 'Only the merge queue merges' in _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/rules/RULES.md and CLAUDE.md with the one-at-a-time landing rule (Brett, Nov 14 2026, his words); decision in _claude/memory/decisions.md; update the merge-queue memory doc; claude-sync sync

before.detail: Root cause: the auto-land builds (auto-land-every-finished-build-lands, auto-land-merge-main-land-land-mjs-clash) finished but never landed, so nothing lands by itself; 87 finished builds sit unlanded, many 1,000-2,000 commits behind main. Do, in order: (1) Land the auto-land code first, combined with replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing: a serial lander that, the moment a build finishes, merges origin/main into it, regenerates generated files (generated-files@1, wire /opt/axf-batch/resolve.py too), runs its checks once and merges it to main; no stacking; a cancelled CI run never counts as a failure; on a red check it files a fix build and moves on. While a build is running, merge main into it every 30 min so it never drifts far behind. (2) Fix the dispatcher: 6 of 8 slots sit empty while builds are queued; find why queued builds don't launch and fix it, with a test. (3) Clear the backlog: land every finished build one at a time, newest and most-wanted first, starting with move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr and change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console (AmberX web app into the console), the console app parts 1-4 and wake listener, and voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected. Builds that are fully superseded get archived (tag archive/<name>) after checking no unique work is lost; anything with unique work gets flagged. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. Send Brett a phone notification with a summary of what landed. Full API and voice, tests, help, Shipped features.

Do, in order: (1) Land the auto-land code first, combined with replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing: a serial lander that, the moment a build finishes, merges origin/main into it, regenerates generated files (generated-files@1, wire /opt/axf-batch/resolve.py too), runs its checks once and merges it to main; no stacking; a cancelled CI run never counts as a failure; on a red check it files a fix build and moves on. While a build is running, merge main into it every 30 min so it never drifts far behind. (2) Fix the dispatcher: 6 of 8 slots sit empty while builds are queued; find why queued builds don't launch and fix it, with a test. (3) Clear the backlog: land every finished build one at a time, newest and most-wanted first, starting with move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr and change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console (AmberX web app into the console), the console app parts 1-4 and wake listener, and voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected. Builds that are fully superseded get archived (tag archive/<name>) after checking no unique work is lost; anything with unique work gets flagged. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. Send Brett a phone notification with a summary of what landed. Full API and voice, tests, help, Shipped features.

# Build: land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-14T22:17:37.935Z
> We need to make sure things are landing as soon as they're built and merged as soon as they're built. I keep getting too many commits behind

## What to build
Continue build "Land on finish: auto-land live, clear backlog" (land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-14 22:17):
"We need to make sure things are landing as soon as they're built and merged as soon as they're built. I keep getting too many commits behind"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (2 left, ~20 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Add 'behind' fields to builds@1 (behindMain count, behindCheckedAt, finishedAt, landState: waiting|landing|landed|red|archived|flagged, landAttempts[]) in framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs + builds-store normaliser, so normBuild keeps them; add a migration that leaves old records untouched; update framework/spec/check-builds-store.mjs cases
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Define land-run@1 record (one serial landing attempt: build, base sha, merged sha, regenerated files, check result, ci conclusion incl. cancelled≠failure, outcome, fixBuild id) as a pure core module with a validator and a fixture
Read first: framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs, framework/cli/builds-store.mjs, framework/spec/check-builds-store.mjs, framework/core/land-run.mjs, framework/spec/fixtures/land-run.json, framework/spec/check-land-run.mjs
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note land-finish-auto-land-live-clear-backlog "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

before.detail: Root cause: the auto-land builds (auto-land-every-finished-build-lands, auto-land-merge-main-land-land-mjs-clash) finished but never landed, so nothing lands by itself; 87 finished builds sit unlanded, many 1,000-2,000 commits behind main. While a build is running, merge main into it every 30 min so it never drifts far behind. (2) Fix the dispatcher: 6 of 8 slots sit empty while builds are queued; find why queued builds don't launch and fix it, with a test. (3) Clear the backlog: land every finished build one at a time, newest and most-wanted first, starting with move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr and change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console (AmberX web app into the console), the console app parts 1-4 and wake listener, and voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected. Builds that are fully superseded get archived (tag archive/<name>) after checking no unique work is lost; anything with unique work gets flagged. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. Send Brett a phone notification with a summary of what landed. Full API and voice, tests, help, Shipped features.

"We need to make sure things are landing as soon as they're built and merged as soon as they're built. I keep getting too many commits behind"
This phase downgrades Fable → Opus: fine, no approval needed (it is recorded when you tick its first step).
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

after.title: Land on finish: auto-land live, clear backlog
after.detail: Root cause: the auto-land builds (auto-land-every-finished-build-lands, auto-land-merge-main-land-land-mjs-clash) finished but never landed, so nothing lands by itself; 87 finished builds sit unlanded, many 1,000-2,000 commits behind main. Do, in order: (1) Land the auto-land code first, combined with replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing: a serial lander that, the moment a build finishes, merges origin/main into it, regenerates generated files (generated-files@1, wire /opt/axf-batch/resolve.py too), runs its checks once and merges it to main; no stacking; a cancelled CI run never counts as a failure; on a red check it files a fix build and moves on. While a build is running, merge main into it every 30 min so it never drifts far behind. (2) Fix the dispatcher: 6 of 8 slots sit empty while builds are queued; find why queued builds don't launch and fix it, with a test. (3) Clear the backlog: land every finished build one at a time, newest and most-wanted first, starting with move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr and change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console (AmberX web app into the console), the console app parts 1-4 and wake listener, and voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected. Builds that are fully superseded get archived (tag archive/<name>) after checking no unique work is lost; anything with unique work gets flagged. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. Send Brett a phone notification with a summary of what landed. Full API and voice, tests, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Own token sets for grids and tab groups
before.detail:
Today grids only have layout tokens (--fx-grid-areas/cols/rows and the -m mobile variants), and tab groups only have --fx-tab-py/--fx-tab-px padding and --fx-tabs-per-row. Both borrow the general colour tokens (--fx-surface, --fx-border, accent), so hover, selected and active states can't be styled on their own. Add dedicated token families in tokens.style, following skins and editable in Token Control, the UI Manager and per instance.
GRID: header background/text/border/sort arrow/filter chip; row, alternate row, hover, selected, focused, expanded, disabled; grid lines, outer border, cell padding, row height, radius; group header, sticky column shadow, empty state; transparency (default 100%).
TAB GROUP: bar background and border; tab text, background and border for idle, hover, active/selected, pressed, disabled and focus ring; active indicator (underline/pill) colour and thickness; badge on tab; fold/overflow button; gap; radius per style (underline, pills, boxed, segmented, plain, chips); transparency (default 100%).
Wire every grid/table and tab group to read them, and add a CI check against hard-coded colours. Per-instance overrides with Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub. Full API. Tests, help, Shipped features. Fable for the token schema.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: it's not just colours. The style variants (tab styles underline/pills/boxed/segmented/plain/chips, grid styles, and every other component's variants) are hard-coded CSS rules with no tokens of their own. Scope is now EVERY component, not just grids and tab groups. Approach, which is additive with no engine or skin rebuild: (1) audit every component and variant in framework/ui/axf.css and the components engine, and list each hard-coded value (radius, border width/style, shadow, padding, gap, font weight/size, indicator thickness, opacity, colours, transitions); (2) give each component its own token family (--fx-<component>-*), and each style variant its own overrides, whose DEFAULT value points at today's general token (e.g. --fx-tab-radius: var(--fx-radius-sm)), so every existing skin looks identical with zero changes; (3) skins and per-instance settings can then override any of them; (4) a CI check that fails on any literal value in component CSS that isn't a token. Show the new tokens in Token Control, the UI Manager and per-instance settings. Fable for the token schema.

Brett: existing skins do not conform to the new component token set. Add a skin migration as the final phase: (1) bump the skin schema version with the new component token families as optional keys, so old skins still validate and fall back to the general tokens; (2) a skin upgrader (CLI + API + a button in the Skins screen) that walks every skin (built-in, professional skins, hub library, user-made) and writes explicit values for every new component token, derived from that skin's own palette and style so it looks deliberate, not just defaulted; (3) run it on every shipped skin in this build and commit the upgraded skins; (4) a CI check that every shipped skin is on the latest schema and covers every component token; (5) the skin builder/AI skin maker must output the full new token set from now on. Show a 'needs upgrade' badge on any skin not on the latest schema.

Brett: scope is ALL FOUR areas for EVERY element: (1) LAYOUTS: placement, size, gaps, columns/rows, alignment, wrap, density, breakpoints; (2) STYLES: radius, borders, shadows, padding, variants, indicators, typography; (3) COLOUR THEMES: every state (idle, hover, active, selected, pressed, focus, disabled, error) light and dark; (4) BEHAVIOUR: transitions/animation timing and easing, hover/press effects, open/close, collapse, scroll, sticky, motion intensity, and reduced-motion. Every one is a token or asset value. Additive defaults point at today's general tokens, so nothing breaks. Split into parallel sub-builds, one per area (layout, style, colour, behaviour), after a shared Fable schema step, then an integration step and the skin upgrader. The CI gate fails on any literal value in any of the four areas. Treat as top priority.

Brett is worried this breaks things. Safety gate: before any change, capture baseline screenshots of every console screen, plugin, dialog, menu, toolbar and tab group (desktop and phone, light and dark, for each shipped skin). After each sub-build, re-capture and pixel-diff. Any difference fails the step and blocks landing until it's fixed (the token defaults must reproduce today's exact look). The engine change is limited to token resolution, and every engine step runs the full test suite. Land the sub-builds one at a time, each behind its own green visual diff.

Brett: EXHAUSTIVE. Every element gets every possible token: every visual or behavioural property that could ever vary is a token, not just the ones in use today. For style, behaviour, colours, layout, typography, spacing, borders, shadows, effects (blur, glass, gradients, opacity), icons, cursor, motion, sound/haptics where relevant, and every state (idle, hover, focus, active, pressed, selected, disabled, loading, error, empty, dragging) in light and dark. Generate the token families from one schema per element type, so a full set is guaranteed and gaps are caught by CI. Defaults still point at today's values, so nothing looks different.

Brett: the full token set will be overwhelming, so add experience-level views wherever skins/tokens/settings are edited (Token Control, the skin builder/config panel, the UI Manager, per-instance settings, Quick settings, the overrides dialog). BASIC: a handful of friendly controls per element (main colour, accent, roundness, density, transparency, animation on/off), each driving many tokens behind the scenes. PRO: grouped by area (colour, style, layout, behaviour) with the common tokens per state. ADVANCED: every single token, raw, searchable and filterable. Every token in the schema carries a 'level' (basic/pro/advanced) and a plain-English description. There is a global level picker plus a per-screen override, remembered per user; a change made in a higher level shows as 'customised' in lower levels. Full API and voice ('switch to advanced view').

before.detail: Root cause: the auto-land builds (auto-land-every-finished-build-lands, auto-land-merge-main-land-land-mjs-clash) finished but never landed, so nothing lands by itself; 87 finished builds sit unlanded, many 1,000-2,000 commits behind main. (2) Fix the dispatcher: 6 of 8 slots sit empty while builds are queued; find why queued builds don't launch and fix it, with a test. (3) Clear the backlog: land every finished build one at a time, newest and most-wanted first, starting with move-amberx-web-app-console-amberx-andr and change-to-move-amberx-web-app-console (AmberX web app into the console), the console app parts 1-4 and wake listener, and voice-listener-use-claude-when-connected. Builds that are fully superseded get archived (tag archive/<name>) after checking no unique work is lost; anything with unique work gets flagged. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. Builds that are fully superseded get archived (tag archive/<name>) after checking no unique work is lost; anything with unique work gets flagged. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. While a build is running, merge main into it every 30 min so it never drifts far behind. (2) Fix the dispatcher: 6 of 8 slots sit empty while builds are queued; find why queued builds don't launch and fix it, with a test. (4) Redeploy the console after each batch of landings (axf-console-update) and check no doubled chrome. (5) Show 'commits behind main' on every build row and alert Brett's phone through AmberX if any finished build sits unlanded more than 15 min. Continue build "Console look becomes default axHub skin" (console-look-becomes-default-axhub-skin) — Phase 1, model Opus.

Brett said (2026-11-14 22:19):
"Keep the design, all the style, the way the console looks right now, and make it the default axHub look, and then make all the apps inherit it right now"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Molly gap: axHub allows Molly's origin on /auth/api/* (CORS with credentials) so native screens read the hub session
before.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. From https://molly.amberxai.com, GET https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/api/session answers 200 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and the preflight OPTIONS /auth/api/logout answers 200 with no CORS headers, so a browser on Molly cannot read the hub session or post a write. The hub should answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins (Molly first) on /auth/api/* with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the origin, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true, Access-Control-Allow-Headers content-type, accept, x-axhub-csrf, Vary Origin; never * with credentials. The session cookie is same-site (SameSite=Lax is enough). Molly side is in place: apps/molly/src/molly/credentials.ts (axhub provider, credentials include, X-AxHub-CSRF on writes).

Only permanent errors (validation, not found) fail, and those send Brett an AmberX FYI with what's missing. Fix the root cause of store.json.lock contention too (stale lock cleanup, short waits for the lock instead of failing). Applies to control_add/set/act, pipeline_queue, console_open/show and all axf-console write tools. Tests: locked store -> call waits/retries and succeeds; session disconnect mid-retry -> still completes.

before.title: Server gate: one session per build, no duplicate launches
before.detail: URGENT, boss order from Brett, Nov 12. The dispatcher double/triple-launched builds: owner-recognized-everywhere ran 3 sessions and molly-gap-console-token-handoff ran 2, in the same worktree folders, clobbering each other and wasting slots. Add a SERVER GATE on the VPS, enforced by the server itself: only ONE live session per build ID and per worktree folder, ever. Every launch path (vps build_start, dispatcher, agent-slots, any claude -p/tmux axf-* launcher) takes an exclusive lock per build ID + folder (flock), and refuses a second launch while a session for that build is alive. A watchdog finds any duplicates that slip through, keeps the oldest, stops the rest, and logs it in 'Automatic fixes' with an AmberX FYI. Also fix the dispatcher's double-launch root cause (see pending dispatcher-a-worktree-store-write-can-erase-a-fr: store write erases the fresh launch record). Tests: second launch of the same build refused; duplicates reaped.

- Collapses vertically with a small handle/arrow button; the handle style is configurable in settings; collapsed state remembered.
- Contents, in order: (1) Skin: shows the current skin; checkbox 'Override console skin' to apply a different skin to just this interface. (2) Default assets for this interface (navigation menu, toolbar, tab group, settings interface, etc.): shows the current asset for each; picker greyed out until 'Override console default' is ticked. (3) Override notice: when anything here overrides the skin or console defaults, show 'This is overriding the current skin/defaults' and reuse the existing 'N assets are controlled by their own settings' (chrome.edits) line that expands to list every override, each with reset.
- Any picked asset must have a manifest and pass schema conformance before applying.
- Reachable by REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help entries, Shipped features.
Works together with the 'all settings interfaces open in a floating dialog' and per-instance settings-window picker builds.

UI Manager (console plugin), opens in a floating window.

- Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1 ('select the main toolbar, set its transparency to 80').
- Elements register via the framework (manifest) so new plugins appear automatically.

before.title: Console app: wake-word voice listener, voice approvals, every console command by voice
before.detail:
Voice control for the console Android app (wrapper, parts 1-4), working offline where possible.
- Always-on wake-word listener, with a wake phrase Brett sets in Settings (several allowed). Runs on-device (offline engine, e.g. Vosk/whisper.cpp + a local intent matcher), with a mic-on indicator and an off switch.
- After the wake phrase the app answers out loud ('What's up?') and listens for a command.
- Voice approvals: 'approve' reads pending approvals one at a time (who asked, what it does); Brett says approve, deny, skip or details. 'Approve all pending' and 'deny all' ask for one spoken confirm. Works from the floating overlay and the lock screen.
- Settings by voice, e.g. 'change the veto timer to two hours' (the axHub veto countdown, so he has that long to veto something before it runs/builds), with the value read back.
- Command catalog: every console action, plugin command, control@1 target and pipeline gets a voice entry, built from the API registry so new plugins appear automatically. Multi-field actions run as a spoken wizard that asks for each missing field ('create a new project' -> 'name?' -> 'Gizmo Johnson' -> confirm). Covers projects, builds/pipelines (file, split, prioritise, land, stop), approvals, settings, tokens/skins, notes/tasks, navigation.
- A Voice commands screen lists every command and its phrasings, searchable, with custom phrases Brett adds.
- Destructive commands always need a spoken confirm.
- Full API parity. Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Own token sets for grids and tab groups
before.detail:
Today grids only have layout tokens (--fx-grid-areas/cols/rows and the -m mobile variants), and tab groups only have --fx-tab-py/--fx-tab-px padding and --fx-tabs-per-row. Both borrow the general colour tokens (--fx-surface, --fx-border, accent), so hover, selected and active states can't be styled on their own. Add dedicated token families in tokens.style, following skins and editable in Token Control, the UI Manager and per instance.
GRID: header background/text/border/sort arrow/filter chip; row, alternate row, hover, selected, focused, expanded, disabled; grid lines, outer border, cell padding, row height, radius; group header, sticky column shadow, empty state; transparency (default 100%).
TAB GROUP: bar background and border; tab text, background and border for idle, hover, active/selected, pressed, disabled and focus ring; active indicator (underline/pill) colour and thickness; badge on tab; fold/overflow button; gap; radius per style (underline, pills, boxed, segmented, plain, chips); transparency (default 100%).
Wire every grid/table and tab group to read them, and add a CI check against hard-coded colours. Per-instance overrides with Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub. Full API. Tests, help, Shipped features. Fable for the token schema.

notes.text: Queued by console.

before.title: Token registry and Skin Editor: live sandbox preview, snapshot history
before.detail:
Runs after the token schema step of own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups (builds on its schema).
1. TOKEN REGISTRY: one registry listing every token in the system, with element type, area (layout/style/colour/behaviour), state, light/dark, level (basic/pro/advanced), plain-English description, default and source. Every new UI, component or plugin MUST register its tokens through its manifest. A CI check fails any UI whose tokens aren't in the registry, and any registered token that nothing uses. Browsable and searchable, with full API.
2. SKIN EDITOR (plugin and screen): pick any UI from the list (a screen, plugin, dialog, element), or pick it on screen, and it's loaded into a sandbox live-preview window with real components and sample data. Every edit hot-renders the preview in real time. The token list comes from the registry, with Basic/Pro/Advanced views. Inline element and asset editors work inside it.
3. DEFAULT SKIN: there is always a built-in default skin that is locked.
4. SNAPSHOTS: every edit to a skin automatically takes a snapshot (like a disk snapshot). A timeline shows the chain of edits, each with time, who/what made it, and a diff of exactly which tokens changed (old -> new). Click any snapshot to preview it, compare any two, or revert to it (a revert is itself a new snapshot, so nothing is ever lost). No breaking skins into separate style or colour groups: the skin is the only unit.
5. EXPORT: at any point, 'Export current to new skin' saves the current state as a brand-new skin (name, thumbnail, to the hub library).
6. Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub work through the snapshots.
7. Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice ('revert the skin to 10 minutes ago', 'export this as a new skin called Midnight'). Tests, help, Shipped features. Fable for the registry and snapshot schema.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: not just individual toolbars, tab groups and menus. Every UI as a whole (each screen, plugin, dialog and app) also gets its own settings interface that changes only that UI, and a DEFAULT STATE: a saved, known-good baseline of its layout, style, colours and behaviour. 'Reset to default' snaps it back, and the default state is itself snapshotted and versioned like skins. Hierarchy: skin -> UI default -> per-UI settings -> per-instance (toolbar/tab group/menu) settings; each level shows what it overrides. Registered in the token registry. Full API and voice.

One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

before.title: Picker dialog plugin replaces all dropdowns
before.detail: New removable plugin: replaces EVERY dropdown/select in the console and framework (native <select>, custom dropdowns, comboboxes) with a tap-to-open picker dialog. The field shows the current value; tapping opens a themed dialog listing the options (search box when many, grouped sections, icons/descriptions if available, multi-select with checkboxes where the select is multiple, keyboard and screen-reader accessible). Fully token-driven: register its own token family (dialog surface, backdrop, option row, selected, hover, focus, search, header, every state, light and dark) in the token registry; no literal colours/sizes (CI gate); every skin can style it and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

For each: fetch its remote branch (pull --rebase or merge the remote branch first; build_land push was rejected as non-fast-forward), merge origin/main, resolve conflicts keeping both sides' features, regenerate generated files (generated-files@1), run tests, push, merge to main. Order: skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land (Skins plugin; installing it hides the built-in skins panel, removing it brings it back), skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land, every-skin-ships-light-dark-colour-theme, console-skin-axhub-only, skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out, skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch, token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups. Archive superseded older branches (skins-plugin-own-removable-console, skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes, professional-skins-rebuild-whole-app, fix-merge-conflicts-pr-557-professional) after checking their commits are included. Then run /usr/local/bin/axf-console-update to redeploy, verify the console loads with no doubled chrome, and send Brett a phone notification through AmberX listing what landed.

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-14T18:15:01.485Z
> land the skin builds

## What to build
Continue build "Land all skin builds" (land-all-skin-builds) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-14 18:15):
"land the skin builds"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

[x] s1 (~6 min) Survey: fetch origin and list the 8 skin branches plus the 4 superseded ones; for each, record ahead/behind vs origin/main, its open PR number and its builds-store record (builds-store.mjs get / builds-live.mjs). Write the table to the top of _claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md and commit it.
[x] s2 (~10 min) skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land: check out the branch, pull --rebase from its remote branch to clear the non-fast-forward, then merge origin/main. Resolve conflicts and keep both sides' features: the Skins plugin hides the built-in skins panel when installed and brings it back when removed. Commit the merge.

[x] s9 (~10 min) console-skin-axhub-only: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the appearance source and skin resolution so the console skin comes only from axHub and per-app skins stay intact. Commit.
[x] s10 (~8 min) console-skin-axhub-only: regenerate the generated files, re-bake the console, run check-skin.mts and the hubstatus tests, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[x] s11 (~10 min) skin-axhub-override-switch-greyed-out: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts with console-skin-axhub-only's switch logic, keeping the greyed-out override plus its reason text. Commit.

[x] s13 (~10 min) skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in skin-switch animations and swatches, keeping the opacity and motion tokens from both sides. Commit.
[x] s14 (~10 min) skin-animations-swatches-skin-switch: regenerate the generated files, run check-theme.mjs, theme-swap.mjs and check-controls.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[x] s15 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox, part 1: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the token registry and control@1 targets: new targets go last, since the registry is append-only. Commit.

[x] s17 (~10 min) token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox: regenerate the fixtures (gen-fixtures.mts), schemas and tracker, re-bake, run check-control, check-skin.mts and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[x] s18 (~10 min) own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: pull --rebase from its remote branch, then merge the previous tip and origin/main. Resolve conflicts in the DataGrid and TabGroup token sets and in the tab-group asset, keeping the token registry entries from both sides. Commit.
[x] s19 (~10 min) own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups: regenerate the generated files, run check-tab-group.mts, check-chrome-assets.mjs, check-theme.mjs and check-skin-coverage.mjs, push, link and add it to the merge queue.
[ ] s20 (~10 min) Brett override: do NOT use the stacked merge queue. Remove the 8 skin PRs from the queue (land.mjs queue remove), then land them one at a time directly in order #647, #648, #590, #618, #641, #652, #657, #654: for each, merge origin/main, regenerate generated files, run its checks once, merge to main (gh pr merge), then the next. If one goes red, fix it on that branch and continue. Record each merge commit in the report.
[ ] s21 (~8 min) Superseded branches: for each of skins-plugin-own-removable-console, skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes, professional-skins-rebuild-whole-app and fix-merge-conflicts-pr-557-professional, list its commits missing from main (git cherry / patch-id). Note any unique work in the report, and stop and flag it instead of archiving if anything real is missing.
[ ] s22 (~6 min) Archive the superseded branches that are fully included: push an archive/<name> tag, delete the remote branch, close their PRs with a note naming the PR that replaced them, and mark their builds-store records complete/superseded.
[ ] s23 (~10 min) Once all 8 have merged, run /usr/local/bin/axf-console-update. Then verify: the console loads, the Skins plugin panel replaces the built-in one with no doubled chrome (one banner, one skins panel), and capture desktop and phone shots with axf shot into the group 'land-all-skin-builds - <Mon D h:mm AM/PM>'.
[ ] s24 (~5 min) Log the deploy with axf_deploy_log (deploy-log@1). Send Brett one phone notification through the AmberX app (axf.notify@1 / alert hub) listing every build that landed with its PR number, and the archived branches.
[ ] s25 (~10 min) Wrap-up: run builds-store.mjs verify and tracker.mjs --check, finish the report (_claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md: order, conflicts resolved, tests, PRs, archived branches, deploy check), and update the THREADS.md row. Mark the build complete in the orchestrator, commit through a status PR into the merge queue, and record the changes.mjs result.
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/land-all-skin-builds.md, _claude/builds/store.json, deploy/, apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step land-all-skin-builds <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link land-all-skin-builds --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step land-all-skin-builds <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. before.title: Picker dialog plugin replaces all dropdowns
before.detail: New removable plugin: replaces EVERY dropdown/select in the console and framework (native <select>, custom dropdowns, comboboxes) with a tap-to-open picker dialog. The field shows the current value; tapping opens a themed dialog listing the options (search box when many, grouped sections, icons/descriptions if available, multi-select with checkboxes where the select is multiple, keyboard and screen-reader accessible). Fully token-driven: register its own token family (dialog surface, backdrop, option row, selected, hover, focus, search, header, every state, light and dark) in the token registry; no literal colours/sizes (CI gate); every skin can style it and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. One shared component used everywhere; plugin off = original dropdowns come back. Works on desktop and phone (bottom sheet style on phone). Full API and voice control (open picker, choose option by name). Tests desktop and phone, help entry, Shipped features.

before.title: Themed native controls plugin
before.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.

after.title: Themed native controls plugin
after.detail: Companion to picker-dialog-plugin-replaces-all, same rules. A removable plugin that replaces every browser-native control in the console and framework with a themed, token-driven version: date/time/datetime pickers -> themed calendar/time dialog; color inputs -> swatch/picker dialog; window.alert/confirm/prompt -> themed dialogs (async API shim); checkboxes, radios, range sliders -> themed switches/radios/sliders; file inputs -> themed drop zone with progress; number inputs -> themed steppers; native title tooltips -> themed tooltips; scrollbars -> themed scrollbars. Each control gets its own token family (every state, light and dark) registered in the token registry; no literal values (CI gate); skins style them and the skin upgrader adds defaults matching today's look. Accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, focus) kept. Each control type can be toggled on/off in the plugin settings; plugin off restores native controls. Desktop and phone (bottom sheets on phone). Full API and voice control. Split into parallel parts per control family. Tests desktop and phone, help, Shipped features.
